headline_marked: [[Probabilistic GNNs]] boost soft robotics maintenance accuracy by 94%
headline: Probabilistic GNNs boost soft robotics maintenance accuracy by 94%
summary: Researchers developed a novel system using Probabilistic Graph Neural Networks to improve diagnostic accuracy for soft robots, outperforming traditional methods.
details: Soft robotics presents unique maintenance challenges due to its deformable nature and distributed sensing, making traditional diagnostic methods insufficient. A new approach leverages Probabilistic Graph Neural Networks (PGNNs) to reason under uncertainty across the robot's interconnected system.

Unlike standard neural networks that treat sensors independently, PGNNs model the soft robot as a graph where nodes represent sensors and edges signify probabilistic physical dependencies. This allows for a more accurate representation of how failures propagate through the material.

The system utilizes message-passing neural networks combined with variational inference to learn a distribution over node states and edge interactions. This probabilistic inference framework enables anomaly detection, root cause analysis, and predictive maintenance.

Implemented using PyTorch and PyTorch Geometric, the PGNN converts raw sensor readings into a graph structure. A key component is the probabilistic message-passing layer, which outputs a Gaussian distribution over node embeddings, propagating uncertainty across the graph.

To address the 'black box' nature of many maintenance systems, the PGNN includes a counterfactual explanation module. This module generates 'what-if' scenarios based on the probabilistic outputs, allowing operators to understand the reasoning behind flagged components.

The system was tested on a bio-inspired soft robotic gripper with 12 pressure sensors and 6 strain gauges. It successfully simulated and detected three types of failures: a slow leak, a sensor malfunction, and a joint blockage.

The PGNN achieved a 94% accuracy (F1 score) in detecting these failures, significantly outperforming a standard GNN (78%) and a feedforward neural network (65%). This demonstrates the power of probabilistic reasoning for complex robotic systems.

Furthermore, the PGNN's ability to provide interpretable explanations through counterfactuals enhances trust and usability in real-world maintenance scenarios. This ethical auditability is crucial for deploying AI in critical robotic applications.

headline_marked: Gamer builds [[booby-trapped Steam Deck]] with taser to stop family
headline: Gamer builds booby-trapped Steam Deck with taser to stop family
summary: A disgruntled gamer has modded their Steam Deck with a 3D-printed spiky case, a taser, and a Raspberry Pi-powered camera and alarm system to deter family members from using it.
details: One gamer, frustrated by family members borrowing their Steam Deck and draining its battery, has taken extreme measures to protect their device. The console has been modified with a 3D-printed case featuring sharp spikes and a built-in taser.

The custom case, designed in Blender, significantly alters the Steam Deck's ergonomics. The owner integrated a Raspberry Pi, a small speaker, an object detection camera, and a servo motor into the setup.

A Python script controls the system: when the camera detects a person in frame, it plays an audio clip. After a short delay, the servo motor triggers the taser, intended to startle and deter unauthorized users.

According to the owner, these anti-sharing measures have been effective, with "nobody touching my Steam Deck anymore." While acknowledging the hassle of removing the case and disarming the taser to use it themselves, they deem it "overall worth it."
The modded Steam Deck now prompts other family members to ask for permission before gaming sessions, a stark contrast to their previous behavior of freely borrowing the device.
